summary: Zhonghui Cui works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where Cui held an attested teaching advisor post in 2013.

Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied under Su Bai from around 1952 to 1956. Zhang served as director at the Palace Museum from around 1987 to 1991.

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. Jiang studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960–1965) and later held posts at Peking University, CASS (~1978–2002 as associate professor), and Soka University (~1999–2000 as visiting researcher).
Zhuan Dao (1871–1943) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. He founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.

Zijie Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 2015). Li was also affiliated with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science as a DC special research fellow (attested 2015).

Zolboo Sandagjav specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at NUM, Delhi, Lausanne, and Bern (2021–2025). Sandagjav held posts at Khan Bank (2011–2015), the UN Mongolian Mission (2020), and as an assistant lecturer at Bern (2024–2025).

Zoltán Gombocz (1877–1935) was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at Berzsenyi Dániel Gimnázium until 1895 and at Eötvös Loránd University between 1895 and 1900.

Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Ganden Shartse and Gyuto monasteries under Trijang Rinpoche and Dechen Nyingpo. He served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse (1937–1946) and led CIHTS (1965; 1967–1971).

Zongsan Mou (1909–1995) was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at Peking University and under Shili Xiong. Mou taught at numerous institutions, including Tunghai University, University of Hong Kong, CUHK, and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies.

Zorya Nikolayevna Petrunicheva (1926–1995) was an Indology scholar who graduated in history from Moscow State University (~1943–1948). In 1953, she held a research position at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Zsigmond Telegdi (1909–1994) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at ELTE, Budapest University of Jewish Studies, and under Émile Benveniste, later serving as Professor of General Linguistics at ELTE from 1958 to 1979.

Zsuzsanna Renner is an Indology and archaeology scholar who completed an MA at Eötvös Loránd University (1978–1986). She held appointments at Central European University (2014), Eötvös Loránd University (2017), and the Archaeolingua Foundation (2017).

Zsóka Gelle is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Berzsenyi Dániel College, ELTE, Manjushree Centre, and University of Vienna, and has held posts at Vienna, Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies, and ELTE, among others.
Zuicho Tachibana (1890–1968) was a scholar in archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He was a student of Kozui Otani (~1907–1914) and Edward Denison Ross (~1910–1912).

Zuiei Ito (1942–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned doctorates from the University of Tokyo and Waseda University. He was a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University from 1980 to 2013.
Zuigan Goto (1879–1965) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Tokyo (1903–1906) and under Sokatsu Shaku (~1906–1914). In 1932, he served as president of Hanazono University.

Zuiho Yamaguchi (1926–2023) studied Tibetology and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo and EPHE under Jacques Bacot and Rolf Alfred Stein. He held positions at CNRS, Toyo Bunko, the University of Tokyo (1970–1986), and Nagoya University (1986).

Zuiryu Nakamura (1915–1997) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and Kenryu Tsukinowa. In 1945, Nakamura was appointed Professor of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University.

Zygmunt Rysiewicz (1911–1954) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Lviv and under Jerzy Kuryłowicz, Louis Renou, Theodor Bloch, and Émile Benveniste, becoming a teacher of comparative linguistics at the University of Warsaw in 1949.
Gyurme tubten nyinje was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.
